extracted.intended_audience: general readers, investors, corporate communicators, compliance officers and journalists interested in corporate fraud and whistleblowing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance-relevant criteria for corporate communications, investor relations and internal compliance in startups and health-tech companies, drawn from the Theranos case. Focuses on what companies should (and should not) do when making technical, clinical and commercial claims and handling whistleblowers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness of public claims and advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Public statements and marketing must accurately reflect product capabilities and partnerships (e.g., Holmes' claims that Theranos tests were used by the US military, or that Edison could run >200 tests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating capabilities or fabricating partnerships. The page documents that false public claims (about scale, partners, validation) led to investor and patient harm and criminal charges; truthful communications help avoid legal, reputational and regulatory consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and regulatory approval before claiming endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not claim validation by regulators or international bodies unless it exists (the article notes Theranos presented claims of FDA and WHO validation that were untrue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only advertise FDA/WHO/regulatory approvals or validations after formal clearance. The Theranos case shows fabricated or misstated regulatory approval (including inserting logos) can be used as evidence of fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about methods, equipment and test procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose how tests are performed, including whether third-party equipment is used (Theranos concealed its use of Siemens equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear with patients, partners and investors about methods and devices used. Concealing reliance on third‑party equipment or disguising methodologies undermines trust and can cause regulatory action and litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical accuracy and clinical reliability before offering tests to patients
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic tests must be reliable and clinically validated before being marketed or used on patients (Edison produced unreliable or false results; only one test—herpes—was FDA-recognized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm clinical accuracy through appropriate validation studies and regulatory pathways prior to commercial deployment. Patient harm from inaccurate results risks severe legal and regulatory consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulating demos, reports or cherry-picking data
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use modified demo devices, hide negative results, or filter data so only 'correct' outputs are shown (Theranos used modified demo devices and filtered out wrong results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure demos, investor materials and reports reflect real-world device performance and include negative/uncertain findings where relevant. Manipulation of demonstrations or reports is a red flag for fraud and can be prosecutable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of data processing and preservation of raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain complete, unaltered records and do not erase or alter erroneous test results (employees documented errors that were ignored; wrong results were erased from evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement auditable data-handling procedures, preserve raw data and error reports, and follow robust change-control/audit trails. Ignoring or deleting unfavorable data invites internal failure and external sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective internal reporting and remediation of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should take employee error reports seriously and investigate (Theranos employees documented problems in error reports that were ignored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish procedures to investigate, remediate and escalate documented technical issues. Ignoring internal reports prevents early fixes and can lead to external whistleblowing and regulatory intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Healthy speak-up culture and whistleblower protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A healthy speak-up culture (e.g., whistleblower hotlines or digital platforms with binding rules) lets employees flag problems without fear; the article contrasts this with Theranos' reprisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide confidential, protected channels for concerns and ensure timely, impartial investigations. Taking tips seriously can prevent scandals; retaliation or disregard leads staff to contact regulators or media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retaliation and respectful treatment of whistleblowers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not threaten, intimidate or surveil employees who raise concerns (Theranos allegedly harassed whistleblowers with private investigators and legal threats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt non-retaliation policies and avoid legal or investigatory tactics that intimidate complainants. Retaliation exacerbates reputational damage and may constitute unlawful conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent operational staffing and qualified technical leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical roles and lab leadership must be filled by personnel with appropriate domain expertise (Theranos had senior operational figures without relevant biomedical experience and later a lab director with no experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure hiring and appointments match responsibilities; board or executive prestige should not substitute for technical competence in operational roles. Misaligned staffing can cause operational failures and mislead stakeholders about capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of conflicts of interest and significant personal relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose material personal relationships and conflicts (Holmes hid her relationship with Balwani from staff and the board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure of relationships that could influence governance or operations is required to preserve trust and comply with governance norms. Undisclosed relationships can impair oversight and enable misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful representation of endorsements, partnerships and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate or misrepresent endorsements, partner validation or corporate affiliations (Theranos added logos of pharmaceutical companies to give impression of approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify and document endorsements and partnership claims before publicizing them. Falsely implying third-party approval is deceptive and can be used as evidence of fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest investor relations and accurate financial representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications to investors must accurately represent company performance and financial projections (Holmes promised much higher company profit than Theranos made).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misleading financial projections and ensure material information is correct. Misrepresenting financials risks SEC action, rescission, and criminal charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory compliance, cooperation and timely disclosure of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with regulators, cooperate with inspections, and disclose material lab or safety violations (CMS inspections revealed shortcomings at Theranos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage proactively with regulatory bodies, remediate violations, and be transparent about risks to patients and consumers. Concealment or non-cooperation invites sanctions, bans and criminal investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor and stakeholder due diligence on technical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Investors and partners should perform rigorous technical and regulatory due diligence instead of relying solely on charismatic promises (defence argued backers failed to research Theranos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct independent validation of technology, request primary data, and verify regulatory status. Rigorous due diligence reduces exposure to fraud risk and informs smarter investment decisions.
